Newly elected commissioners Wendy Jacobs and Fred Foster Jr. joined returning incumbents Michael D. Page, Ellen W. Reckhow, and Brenda A. Howerton, as interim appointees Pam H. Karriker and Rev. meetings.title: 2013 State of Durham County - by Fred Foster, Chairman of BOCC
meetings.executive_summary: Chairman Fred Foster Jr. delivered the 2013 State of Durham County address in a prerecorded broadcast format, highlighting national community accolades, new county leadership appointments, county rebranding, and the completion of the 11-story courthouse and parking deck. Looking ahead to the FY 2014 budget and the FY 2014–2023 Capital Improvement Program, Foster warned of uneven economic recovery, federal sequestration cuts, and state-level reductions including potential shifts in school construction lottery funds. Responding to a county manager and staff recommendation for a significant property tax rate increase to cover debt service on new county buildings, Foster urged internal efficiency reviews and potential service adjustments to minimize or avoid a tax increase while maintaining the county's AAA bond rating and core commitments to Durham Public Schools, vulnerable residents, transportation, and public safety. Because this was a solo broadcast report, no formal board motions or votes took place.

agenda_items.title: Opening Remarks, Community Accolades, and County Leadership Highlights
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chairman Fred Foster Jr. opens the 2013 State of Durham County address in a broadcast format and highlights national recognitions for Durham, including a New York Times feature, ranking #1 large county best positioned for growth in 2012 by the Fourth Economy Community Index, Duke University's national ranking, and R.N. Harris Elementary School's 2012 National Excellence in Urban Education Award. He recognizes new department leaders—HR Director Cora Wilson, a new Veterans Services Director, and DSS Director Michael Beckets—as well as peer honors for Deputy County Manager Lee Worsley, Tax Administrator Kimberly Simpson (noting a 98.86% tax collection rate), and Public Health Director Gayle Harris. Foster also highlights Durham County's new branding replacing the historic seal and the launch of a modernized website at www.dconc.gov.

agenda_items.title: Capital Projects and FY 2014–2023 Capital Improvement Program (CIP)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Foster reviews major capital accomplishments, led by the completion of the new 11-story courthouse and adjacent parking deck, which began court operations on February 11 and held its formal dedication on March 10, also housing the Durham County Sheriff's Department. He notes ongoing capital projects including the final phase of the Human Services Building, refurbishment of the vacant judicial building, storage facilities, technology upgrades, and land acquisition. Reviewing the FY 2014–2023 Capital Improvement Program presented on March 7, Foster notes a recent collaborative meeting with the Board of Education regarding Durham Public Schools' facility needs and future bond timing, with BOCC expected to finalize the CIP later in the month.

agenda_items.title: Economic Outlook, Federal Sequestration, and State Budget Impacts
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Foster describes an uneven economic recovery, noting Durham County's 7.5% unemployment rate (slightly below the 7.7% national average) alongside North Carolina's unemployment rate ticking up from 9.4% to 9.5%, and citing budget retreat insights from NC State economist Dr. Michael Walden. He highlights uncertainty surrounding the March 1 federal sequester ($85 billion in federal cuts affecting mental health, Head Start, unemployment benefits, food safety, and emergency disaster response). At the state level, he notes the Governor's March belt-tightening directives tied to Medicaid debt and a two-year state budget proposal under which school construction lottery funding is expected to remain below statutory levels and face reallocation to school technology and pre-K slots, leaving Durham County to absorb cuts to state-mandated programs.

agenda_items.title: FY Budget Priorities, Debt Service, and Property Tax Rate Directive
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Addressing the upcoming budget cycle, Foster notes that the County Manager and staff have recommended a significant property tax rate increase earmarked to pay debt service on newly constructed county buildings. While affirming the county's commitment to meeting debt obligations and preserving its AAA bond rating, Foster states he is asking the County Manager and staff to look internally for savings and evaluate service efficiencies—including difficult choices to cut back some service levels—to reduce or eliminate the proposed tax rate increase. He concludes by affirming core funding priorities for Durham Public Schools operations and capital needs, youth and senior services, natural and built resources, job-creating economic development, transportation infrastructure, and public health and safety.
